title: Give the Meeting a Facilitator draft 4 - "don't go overboard" (no rush)
summary:
Your Nov 16 note applied: "Want to make sure that it is clear to not go overboard with this pattern. A big part of meetings needs to remain relationship building." New in draft 4: a line in the lead ("more time for the people in them, not less"); a **Don't go overboard** paragraph after the Problem; **Leave room for people** in Step 1 (keep the first few minutes for catching up - no clock, no agenda, no notes; more jobs is not a better facilitator) and a menu row; the social side in What stays with people; a Measure-it check (ask people whether meetings still feel like time with their colleagues - if it drops, dial it back); a Notes item; a prompt rule.

**Value line:** "For example, arranging meetings and keeping calendars is work an administrative assistant does - the nearest match, secretaries and administrative assistants, is a role that pays a median of about $48,310 a year, and an executive administrative assistant about $76,590 (Bureau of Labor Statistics, May 2025, pay only, not benefits)." From the Nov 16 4 PM check.
